name: Nottingham Forest 1978/79-1979/80 (Brian Clough, two European Cups)
scopeNote: Nottingham Forest under Brian Clough from the first league match of 1978/79 (home 1-1 v Tottenham, 19 August 1978, taken from a search summary) to the 1980 European Cup final win over Hamburg (28 May 1980). The 12 August 1978 Charity Shield (5-0 v Ipswich) is treated as an exhibition and excluded. Includes the 1979 final (Malmo, 30 May 1979) and the 1980 final. Peter Taylor was assistant, mentioned in evidence only. The 1977/78 title season is out of period: facts about it (4-3-3, Shilton and Burns signings) are kept unverified. Sources call the style simple and direct, built on a solid defence, Robertson's crossing and counter-attacks; no source here uses 'zonal' or 'man-marking' for the side. Tactical coverage is thin and mostly retrospective (players' interviews, tier B-C); no tier A tactical study was found.
openQuestions: No source found describing the marking system (zonal vs man); only Burns/Lloyd on Keegan in 1980 is documented.
Shape in 1978-80 (4-4-2 vs 4-3-3) not verified in period; the only 4-3-3 mention is for 1977/78 and FM sites claim 4-4-2.
Pressing is not documented for this side.
Start date of the first competitive match (19 Aug 1978) and the Charity Shield date (12 Aug 1978) come from a search summary and Wikipedia knowledge, not a mined page.
The 1979 first-leg quote date (11 April 1979 v Cologne) is from memory.
Whether the 1980 final was played with a 4-4-2 or five across midfield: only the blog states five in midfield after Mills dropped back.
